newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairies to see little rain to June 20-EC.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairies to see little rain to June 20-EC.

text.p: Canada's Prairies on Friday were forecast to see little rain through to June 20, Environment Canada meteorologist Francois Choquette said.
"Generally, it'll stay pretty dry. We saw the same scenario last weekend and we barely got any rain," Choquette said in French. "It's not good for anyone who wants rain."
Wheat yield prospects were reduced by 0.5 bushels an acre on Wednesday due to drought conditions on southeastern Prairie crops, a Canadian Wheat Board weather analyst said.
Typical yields on Prairie wheat ranges from 30 to 32 bu/ac and were reduced on Wednesday to 29.5 to 31.5 bu/ac.

Southeast Saskatchewan and southwestern Manitoba farmland usually produces more wheat than the Prairie average at between 32 to 35 bu/ac because droughts occur less frequently there than in southern Alberta and the land is black soil which is richer than south Alberta's brown soil, the CWB said.

Alberta may see five to 10 mm (0.4 inch) in thundershowers Friday. Two to five mm (0.2 inch) of rain may fall in parts of Saskatchewan Saturday and up to 10 to 15 mm (0.6 inch) over Manitoba's Interlake region on Sunday, Choquette said.
"Temperatures should be at or above normal, warming through the weekend and into next week," Choquette added.
"The U.S. weather models show us hot and dry to June 20."
The normal Prairie high now is 26 Celsius (78.8 F).
